title: Quote shell parameter expansions used as command arguments
why: An unquoted parameter expansion can split one value into multiple arguments and expand wildcard characters into filesystem paths.
suggestion: Quote scalar expansions, forward positional arguments with "$@", or use an array when intentional argument splitting is required.
limitations: Assignment, quoted, double-bracket conditional-test, arithmetic, and shell grammar contexts where word splitting does not apply are excluded.
Named parameters and the exact forwarding forms $@, $*, ${@}, and ${*} are recognized; individual positional parameters such as $1 and operators on special parameters are not resolved.
At most one representative finding is reported per file and it is advisory by default.
Variable values, arithmetic assignment success, and earlier validation are not resolved, so numeric-looking parameters are not assumed safe.
Intentional splitting through legacy scalar variables cannot be distinguished from accidental splitting.
